title: The Dragon with Many Heads and the Dragon with Many Tails
text:
In La Fontaine's fable, an envoy of the Ottoman sultan was at the court of the Holy Roman Emperor, and the Germans there were boasting about their empire's power. Their emperor, one of them said, had so many princes and lords under him, each with an army of his own, that he could field more troops than any other ruler.

The envoy answered with a story. He had once seen, he said, a dragon with a hundred heads trying to pass through a hedge. Each head wanted to go its own way. One head pushed through here and another there, and the body was held back. The whole creature got stuck, and it could not get through at all.

Then, he said, he had seen another dragon, with only one head but a hundred tails. That head chose a gap in the hedge, went through, and the body and every one of the hundred tails followed easily behind it.

The envoy's point was clear. The Germans' empire was the first dragon. His own master's empire, with a single head to command it, was the second.
lesson: Many strong members do not make a strong team if each one wants to lead in a different direction. Agree on who decides, and a large group can move through a narrow gap.
people: An envoy of the sultan, German courtiers
location: France (story set at the imperial court)
source: Jean de La Fontaine, Fables, Book I, The Dragon with Many Heads and the Dragon with Many Tails, 1668
